page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native family server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 4 vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is configured with a shared CPU allocation. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2 instruction sets. The server is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, providing 6.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, but comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a mixed performance profile. The shared AMD EPYC processor delivers poor single-core performance in stress-ng testing, placing in the bottom 10%, and weak multi-core performance in the bottom 25%. However, Geekbench testing shows average performance in the middle 50% for single-core and multi-core workloads, as well as software compilation and ray tracing. Memory performance is also split; while the PassMark memory score falls in the bottom 10%, the cached read-only small block memory bandwidth reaches an average tier of 411.67 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations both register in the weak bottom 25% category, with Redis handling 5.87 million operations per second.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this instance offers a budget-friendly resource density for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is suitable for basic web serving, lightweight text processing, and software compilation tasks that can tolerate variable CPU availability. The 24.0 GB memory capacity provides sufficient headroom for moderate memory-bound applications, though the weak database and Redis benchmark results suggest it is less suited for high-throughput transactional databases or intensive real-time data stores.
